x: We welcome to the Club as new members, David Stevens, E. Froude (2nd claim), Denis Squires and Ray Switzer and hope that they will enjoy our company and turn out regularly at Battersea and at Wimbledon during the winter.

Froude and D, Stevens gave a forward display and our two veterans Charlie Speechley and Bert East battled bravely through to the end. Owing to the time taken to collect and carry the china, etc. which had been won, we were late for a little celebration with some of the ladies, plus the President, hi…
Ray Switzer, ably backed up by Ray Hall, Dave Stevens and Eric Froude gained his 7 mile badge in this section. Peak of this meeting, is the "A" section, and we saw a grand performance by our lads.

Ray Middleton, home from Ireland, walked well to finish 6th in 41m.21s., Dave Stevens (individual) was 7th, Nick Milsum 9th and Terry Clark, who walked a blinder on the last lap, was 12th and Trevor Luck 13th.
Chiefly due to a clash with the Stock Exchange 7 miles championships, only 29 walkers started, and we were without Stan Vickers, Ray Hall and Dave Stevens.

This was no doubt due to the fact that on the same day there occured the Police Sergeant's examination and the Stock Exchange championship. The latter event was won by Stan Vickers with Ray Hall second and Dave Stevens sixth. The match resulted in a win for us by 33 pts. to 72.

Such was my fortune and pleasure in witnessing one of our younger school display such fine characteristics and have his name added to the long list of champions this Club has produced. Congratulations also to Dave Stevens for his performance in finishing fourth.
After a tough battle a comfortable win was recorded by a softly handicapped Stevens of Steyning. Carl Lawton was 3rd, producing an estimated P.B. for 3,000m.
